answer: A beacon binds each identity to a zero-knowledge proof of personhood, while a verifiable delay function imposes sequential puzzles that forged identities cannot cross the temporal ridge without paying real time. Staking collateral locks deposits, slashing penalties burn bonds on duplicated oracles, and zero-knowledge attestations keep credentials private yet auditable. The attack has negative expected utility because cloning is slow, expensive, and slashable, yielding a robust Nash equilibrium at the protocol summit.
